population.note: FICTIONAL ESTIMATES. Arithmetic, in % of US adults: current 14.9 = 9.0 never-stopped (many of them diabetes patients or 2027–28 starters who have not yet hit the one-year mark) + 5.9 restarters; ever 21.0 − current 14.9 = 6.1 off now, of whom ~1.3 had already restarted once. Cycled = (5.9 + 1.3)/21 ≈ 34%. Ever-stopped = 5.9 + 6.1 = 12.0, i.e. 57% of ever-users, which fits roughly one-third one-year persistence once you allow for recent starters. Restarted/ever-stopped = 7.2/12.0 ≈ 60%. That is a multi-year cumulative figure, above the 36–47% restart rate within one year. The 2027 injectable shortage pushed about 1 pp off therapy, and about half of them returned on orals. Income thirds weight to about 14.8. Bottom third rose slowest: employer exits fell mostly on hourly workforces, and the HRSA free-provision programme (520k enrolled) only partly offsets that. Age bands weighted by adult population (~20/33/24/23%) give ~15.0. 65+ rose from 9% to 13% because of the Medicare Bridge (~2.1M obesity-indication enrollees). Never-users who cannot get it: about 79% of adults have never used, and among adults with obesity roughly 3 in 5 have never used. Pediatric: ~0.7% of under-18s (~510k), mostly 12–17. Ages 6–11 peaked at ~70k after the Aug 2027 label, and new starts in that group are down ~30% since the Aug 2028 growth safety communication. Medicaid EPSDT has narrowed the income skew among children, but it has not reversed it.

access.public_coverage: Medicare GLP-1 Bridge extended by CMMI to Dec 2029 after Congress again failed to legislate permanent Part D obesity coverage. Terms unchanged: Medicare pays ~$245/month, copay ~$50. About 2.1M enrollees on the obesity indication: 2.1M × $245 × 12 ≈ $6.2B/yr gross federal cost, which runs ahead of the CBO's ≥$35B/9-yr (~$3.9B/yr) original score. Medicaid: 17 states cover adult obesity at the $245 rate and 6 that tried it dropped it on budget grounds. Children: under EPSDT, Medicaid must cover Wegovy for medically necessary paediatric obesity, including ages 6–11 since Aug 2027. HRSA Community Metabolic Health Program (launched Jan 2028) gives free oral GLP-1 (Foundayo or oral Wegovy) to uninsured adults ≤200% FPL with BMI ≥35, or ≥30 plus a comorbidity, at federally qualified health centres. Funding is $3B over FY2028–29. Enrollment is 520k at a federal purchase price of $149/month: 520k × $149 × 12 ≈ $0.93B/yr run-rate, and FY2028 outlays are ~$0.6B because of the ramp.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 60+ brands at ~$8–40/month. Canada: generic semaglutide at ~CAD 70–110, and several provinces now fund it publicly. Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and much of Southeast Asia have generics. Generic injectable semaglutide is available in ~160 countries. Generic tirzepatide is not yet available anywhere major.
access.note: The price shock comes from supply. In Apr 2027 an FDA warning letter and a lot recall at a Novo fill-finish plant put semaglutide injection back on the FDA shortage list until Feb 2028. Novo suspended its $349 new-start cash offer for injectable Wegovy. Injectable cash prices for new starts rose to ~$499 via telehealth. Lilly raised Zepbound vial cash pricing from $349–499 to $399–549, citing demand and onshoring costs. The oral $149 starter price lapsed with the deal's 24-month launch window (Jan 2028), so cash orals now cost $199–399; HRSA buys at $149. 503B compounding of these drugs has been barred since the exclusion was finalised in Dec 2026, but the shortage legally reopened 503A compounding for ten months. Compounded product plus personal importation of Indian and Canadian generic semaglutide make the gray market an estimated 8–10% of US users. Employer coverage for weight management fell to 44% (Business Group on Health, 2027–28) and now clusters on T2D, cardiovascular-event and sleep-apnoea codes. Route: weekly injectables are still about half of dispensed volume, but ~60% of 2028 new starts are oral.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg and 50 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
GLP-1/amylin combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema, approved Dec 2026)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: alcohol use disorder: confirmatory phase 3 under way, still not approved; addiction clinics prescribe off-label
microdosing for 'metabolic health' via telehealth, much of it compounded during the shortage
paediatric use under 6 and use in non-obese children, rare and specialist-only
drugs.pipeline_note: Oral parity is realised through a new strength of an existing product. A head-to-head trial (published Nov 2027) found oral semaglutide 50 mg daily non-inferior to injectable Wegovy 2.4 mg, at ~15% vs ~15% loss at 68 weeks. The FDA approved the 50 mg pill in Mar 2028. The pill now matches the semaglutide needle, but not tirzepatide (~21%). It also needs roughly 100× the API per patient-month of the injection, which caps supply. CagriSema was approved Dec 2026 but has modest uptake after its REDEFINE-4 miss. Retatrutide's BLA was filed Mar 2027; an advisory committee on the dysesthesia signal is scheduled, and an FDA decision is expected early 2029, so it is not on the market. Amycretin is in phase 3 with readouts 2029. Survodutide was filed in 2028. MariTide monthly is in phase 3, and bimagrumab adjuncts are in phase 2. Neither is on the US market.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Rates on oral 50 mg are similar to the injection.
No causal confirmation in long-term data; absolute risk low.
~25–30% of weight lost is lean mass. A bone-density signal in older adults is now replicated in two cohorts, so Medicare Bridge enrollees are the population of concern.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No label change. Several Medicare Advantage plans pair coverage with resistance-training benefits.
EMA 'very rare' label; FDA added a postmarketing adverse-reaction mention in 2027 without a class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Clinically meaningful in an estimated 1–3% of users, dose-related and usually reversible on dose reduction, according to 2027 pharmacovigilance analyses and one prospective cohort. Milder blunting is self-reported by more users, but this is not well measured.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed as an uncommon adverse reaction (apathy, anhedonia) on the oral Wegovy 50 mg label (Mar 2028); class-wide label harmonisation is under review.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The shortage was a natural experiment. Shortage-forced stoppers regained ~50–60% of lost weight within 12 months, which is closer to the trial figure than to the 2026 real-world claims.
Iron, B12 and vitamin D deficits are reported in long-term users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance recommends baseline labs; no label.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects of decades-long use from adolescence; effects of repeated cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About six years of RCT and extension follow-up now exist. Shortage-era cycling is being studied in claims data.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements on all new approvals.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FDA adverse-event reports tied to compounded or imported product passed ~3,400 after the 2027 shortage reopened 503A compounding. Contaminated imported vials were found in two states.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: 503B exclusion finalised Dec 2026. Warning letters resumed when the shortage ended in Feb 2028, and import alerts were placed on several Indian online sellers.

safety_ledger.effect: Paediatric growth and psychiatric signal in children who started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: In a multi-site US paediatric EHR cohort (May 2028), prepubertal children on semaglutide for ≥12 months grew ~0.8 cm/yr more slowly than BMI-matched controls. The comparison is confounded by puberty timing and by the effect of weight loss itself on growth. Separately, restrictive-eating diagnoses (ARFID/anorexia) were ~1.6× higher in children who started before age 14. Absolute numbers are small, and no RCT has had the power to test either finding.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA Drug Safety Communication (Aug 2028) requires height and pubertal staging every 6 months and an eating-disorder screen. A PREA growth study is required. EMA PRAC review is open. The AAP issued interim guidance urging caution under age 10.

food_and_beverage.state: GLP-1 households are ~27% of US households. US salty-snack and confectionery volumes are down ~3–4% over two years, and the main brands are holding revenue through price-pack architecture and protein-forward SKUs. A small 'full-appetite' counter-niche (heritage baking, 'real portion' packaging) is marketed at the unmedicated movement in Austin and other Sun Belt metros.

alcohol.state: US spirits depletions are down ~5% across 2027–28. Distillers attribute part of it to GLP-1s, along with Gen Z abstention. Premium single-serve and non-alcoholic lines are growing but do not make up the volume lost at the heavy-drinker end.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat and check sizes smaller. 'Half-portion' menus are standard at casual-dining chains. Some independents in Austin and Nashville advertise 'unmedicated portions' as a marketing line.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep contracting: Torrid has closed ~180 stores and DXL is shrinking its fleet. Mainstream retailers carry more mid sizes. The size-down re-buying wave has slowed.

fitness.state: Muscle-preservation programmes are standard, and some Medicare Advantage plans reimburse strength classes. Natural-bodybuilding federations and a few amateur leagues have added GLP-1s to drug-tested lists, which is now a marketing niche.

insurance.state: Employer weight-management coverage is down to 44%, and retail, hospitality and logistics employers have exited most. Those still covering use BMI ≥35 or require a cardiometabolic code, step through orals first, and impose 24-month caps. Pharmacy trend is around +9%. Diabetes and CVD coverage is untouched.

pharma.state: Lilly has widened its lead: Novo's 2027 plant failure cost it injectable share, though oral Wegovy 50 mg won some of it back. Supply of oral peptide API is the industry's new bottleneck. The global incretin market is ~$110B in 2028. Ex-US prices are collapsing while US cash prices rise.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Thinness is still read as 'on it'. There is now a counter-signal: visible appetite, and the phrase 'unmedicated' on dating profiles, gym shirts and menu cards.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Two tiers. Salaried workers with large-employer plans, and Medicare enrollees, get covered drugs. Hourly workers lose coverage and pay $199–499 cash, use the gray market, or go without, unless they are poor enough and uninsured enough for HRSA. Working-poor families with Medicaid children now have kids on Wegovy while the parents are uncovered.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: In GLP-1 households, smaller plates are the default. The unmedicated movement has made shared, abundant meals a deliberate performance: Sunday bread, long tables, 'eat in public' meetups.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Some dating apps now carry an optional 'on / off / unmedicated' field. Couples who are 'mismatched', one on and one off, are a common advice-column subject.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Clinic culture treats appetite as a treatable signal. The movement treats it as evidence of being yourself. The paediatric growth signal hands the movement its strongest argument: leave children's appetites alone.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: Acknowledged as uncommon, roughly 1–3% clinically meaningful, dose-related and reversible. It is now on one label and in clinic intake questionnaires (PHQ-style apathy screens at titration visits).
interior_life.framing: Side effect, handled like an adjustable dose. Addiction medicine frames the same mechanism as treatment, and the unmedicated movement frames it as character loss ('they want you calm').
interior_life.effect_on_work: There is no employer encouragement. Some EAPs offer guidance for staff who report flatness. A few anecdotes from sales and creative roles describe lost drive, and occupational health clinicians treat it as a dose question.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Musicians and comics talk about adjusting dose before tours. A minor genre of personal essays ('the year I couldn't love sour candy') has emerged. Nothing measurable at population scale.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Clinics ask about libido and connection at follow-up. Couples counsellors report cases where one partner's blunting is mistaken for falling out of love.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: No measurable effect on users. Anhedonia has become rhetoric: unmedicated and wellness-populist voices use it against the HRSA subsidy ('sedating the poor'), and it splits the administration's own health coalition.

state.regulatory_posture: Still pro-access and fast: the oral 50 mg was approved on schedule and the paediatric label granted. FDA enforcement against compounders resumed after the shortage, and paediatric safety is now being acted on with monitoring requirements rather than restriction.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Direct subsidy: HRSA gives oral GLP-1s free to low-income uninsured adults (520k enrolled; $3B FY2028–29). The Medicare Bridge is extended to 2029 at $245/$50. Medicaid EPSDT covers children. There is no mandate. Congress has not created permanent Medicare obesity coverage.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: HRSA enrollment requires quarterly weight and adherence check-ins to keep the free supply. Paediatric prescribing now requires growth monitoring every 6 months. Employer plans use step therapy and duration caps.
state.workforce_or_military: None formal. DoD TRICARE covers on cardiometabolic codes only, and recruiting standards are unchanged.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: US exclusivity runs to ~2031–32. The US–India price gap (~$399 vs ~$15) is now a talking point in Congress. Several states have petitioned FDA over importing Canadian generic semaglutide, with no approvals. Novo's 2027 plant failure exposed concentrated fill-finish capacity, and peptide API for the 50 mg pill is tight. Lilly's US small-molecule plants for orforglipron are the most resilient supply.

events.event: FDA warning letter and recall of Wegovy/Ozempic pen lots from a Novo fill-finish plant. Semaglutide injection returns to the FDA shortage list for ten months, Novo suspends its $349 new-start cash offer, and 503A compounders legally resume.
FDA approves Wegovy injection for children aged 6–11 with obesity on the basis of the STEP Young trial. Medicaid EPSDT coverage follows automatically.

Business Group on Health survey: 44% of large employers now cover GLP-1s for weight management, down from 60%. Most remaining plans restrict coverage to diabetes, cardiovascular or sleep-apnoea codes, or to BMI ≥35.
HRSA launches a $3B free-provision programme giving oral GLP-1s to uninsured low-income adults at community health centres. CMS extends the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge to Dec 2029 at $245/$50.
FDA approves oral Wegovy 50 mg after a head-to-head trial shows it is non-inferior to the weekly injection. The label lists apathy and anhedonia as uncommon adverse reactions.

FDA Drug Safety Communication on slower height growth and higher restrictive-eating diagnoses in children who started GLP-1s young. It requires growth monitoring every six months, and new paediatric starts fall ~30%.

open_tensions: Two-tier access is hardening. The state pays for the poorest uninsured, Medicare enrollees and Medicaid children. Employers have walked away from the hourly middle, who pay rising cash prices or buy Indian generics, and no one has proposed covering them.

The paediatric growth signal is confounded and unresolved. Thousands of children are on a drug that requires six-monthly height checks, and their parents can't tell whether stopping risks regain or continuing risks height.

The oral pill matches the needle on efficacy but uses ~100× the API. Oral parity has moved the supply bottleneck rather than removed it, and a second plant failure would hit the subsidised oral programmes first.
The unmedicated movement and the administration's own wellness base oppose the subsidy the administration funds. Anhedonia, now on a label, has become a political argument.
still_true: Wegovy's US list price is $1,349 per month, and almost nobody pays it.
There is no FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US; exclusivity runs to roughly 2031–32.
Medicare pays ~$245/month with a ~$50 beneficiary copay under the GLP-1 Bridge (now extended).
The FDA's January 2026 removal of the suicidal-ideation warning stands; the association remains debunked.
Generic semaglutide in India sells for roughly $8–48 per month.

prose.headline: The Pill Caught Up With the Needle. Your Employer Didn't. Your Kid's Pediatrician Is Measuring His Height Again.
prose.world_in_600_words:
By late 2028 about one American adult in seven takes an incretin drug, and one in five has taken one at some point. The space between those two numbers is a population: people who stopped because of side effects, because a benefit was capped, or because the pharmacy had nothing to dispense in the summer of 2027. Many of them have started again since. A third of everyone who has ever used these drugs has gone off and come back at least once. Cycling is no longer a deviation from the treatment. It is the treatment as most people live it.

The shortage changed things more than any launch. In April 2027 a fill-finish plant failed inspection and semaglutide pens went back on the federal shortage list. Novo stopped its cash discount for new patients. Telehealth injectable prices climbed toward five hundred dollars, and for ten months compounding pharmacies were legally back in business. People who were cut off regained most of what they had lost within a year. That settled an argument the 2026 claims data had left open. By the time pens returned, the pill was ready. In March the FDA approved a 50-milligram daily semaglutide tablet that matched the weekly injection head to head. Most people starting in 2028 start on a pill. It is not cheaper to make. Each patient-month takes about a hundred times the active ingredient a pen does, so the bottleneck has moved from needles to peptide supply.

Coverage has split in two. Fewer than half of large employers still pay for weight loss, and those that do want a diabetes or heart code, a BMI of thirty-five, or a two-year limit. Retail, logistics and hospitality employers have mostly left. The state, meanwhile, has stepped in at both ends of the income scale. The Medicare pilot was extended at its original price, and about two million older adults now get the drug for fifty dollars a month. A new federal programme hands out oral pills free at community health centres to half a million uninsured people with low incomes. The people in the middle, hourly workers without the right diagnosis, pay two to four hundred dollars a month, order vials from India, or go without. In Texas a home health aide can be on a free government pill while her colleague with insurance cannot get one.

Children sit inside this. Since August 2027 Wegovy has been approved down to age six, and Medicaid has to cover it when it is medically necessary. That briefly evened the old income skew among children. Then in May a large paediatric records study found that young children on the drug were growing almost a centimetre a year more slowly than their peers. Children who started before fourteen also had more restrictive-eating diagnoses. The study cannot separate the drug from weight loss or puberty timing. The FDA now requires height checks every six months, and new paediatric prescriptions have fallen by about a third.

The flattening that people called 'Ozempic personality' in 2026 now has a line on a label: apathy, anhedonia, uncommon. Clinics ask about it at titration visits and lower the dose, and most patients recover. For the clinic it is a dosing problem. Politically it has become a slogan.

The slogan belongs to the unmedicated: young adults in Austin and Nashville, homesteading parents, natural bodybuilders, some fat-acceptance activists who resent employer pressure. They wear the word on shirts, set long tables on Sundays, and object to the subsidy as sedating the poor. Their politics overlap uncomfortably with those of the administration that funds the subsidy. Snack volumes are down a few percent, spirits are contracting, and plus-size chains are closing stores. From the outside nothing looks broken.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Marisol Treviño takes her pill at 5:40 with half a glass of water and then waits thirty minutes before coffee, because the clinic nurse said so twice. It is a white tablet from the health centre on Zarzamora Street, free, and the bottle has a sticker with her quarterly check-in date. She has eleven days until it.

She drives to Mr. Ochoa's house, then to Mrs. Garza's. Mrs. Garza's son is on Zepbound through the refinery. He asks whether hers is the government one, the way people ask whether your phone is the free kind.

At two she picks up Ana, ten, for the pediatric appointment. The letter came in September, something about growth. The medical assistant measures Ana against the wall twice and writes 134.6. Last March it was 132.1. The doctor does math on a screen and says it's within range, probably, and asks whether Ana is eating lunch. Ana says yes. Marisol knows about the tortillas wrapped back into foil.

The doctor offers to lower the dose. Marisol asks what happens if they stop. The doctor tells her honestly that Ana would likely gain it back, and that nobody knows yet about the height.

In the car her sister in Austin has texted a photo of a long table, bread torn open, twelve people laughing, the caption *unmedicated sunday*. Marisol hearts it.

At dinner Ana eats half her rice and asks for the sour gummies. Marisol gives her three, eats one herself, and can't tell whether it tastes like it used to.

least_plausible_claims.why: magnitude: the 2026 base was ~0.6% of children with obesity (roughly 90k children). A rise to ~510k implies about a sixfold jump in two years, and 0.7% of all under-18s implies roughly 3–4% of children with obesity, with no mechanism for the adolescent surge beyond the under-12 label.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Business Group on Health survey: 44% of large employers now cover GLP-1s for weight management, down from 60%.
least_plausible_claims.why: magnitude: a 16-point fall in one survey year is steeper than the 12-point fall in 2025–26. The text asserts it with no cost trigger beyond 'employer retreat', and the ~$499 cash-price rise points the other way for employer cost pressure.

least_plausible_claims.quote: It requires growth monitoring every six months, and new paediatric starts fall ~30%.
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: a ~30% fall in new starts is dated to the same month as the Drug Safety Communication, so the effect appears at once with no chain through prescribers, Medicaid or parents. The underlying growth signal is also described as confounded.

rationale.badness: A recognisably harder society with new losers. Hourly workers sit in a hardening middle tier, paying $199–499 cash or using a gray market of 8–10% of users with ~3,400 adverse-event reports and contaminated imports. Children on Wegovy face an unresolved growth and restrictive-eating signal while their parents go uncovered. It is not worse than that, because the state backstops the poor and Medicare enrollees, anhedonia is measured and labelled (1–3%, reversible), and the harms are nameable, which lowers the epistemic score.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Every driver is visible in fields and events: the shortage price shock, 44% employer coverage, the 6–11 label, the growth signal, the oral 50 mg, the unmedicated movement, the HRSA subsidy and niche anhedonia. The Novo plant failure sits slightly uneasily with market_shock 'none', though it is the price_path mechanism. mechanism: Most chains are shown, including the shortage leading to compounding, the regain natural experiment, oral API demand and bottleneck, and Bridge enrollment leading to 65+ uptake. Weaker links are the same-month 30% drop in paediatric starts and the 16-point employer drop (claims 2 and 3), plus the label change appearing only on the 50 mg pill. magnitude: Adult on-drug (14.9), ever-used (21), income thirds (~14.8 weighted) and age bands (~15.0 weighted) are inside the envelope and reconcile, as do the cycling arithmetic, Medicare ($6.2B), HRSA ($0.93B) and approval timing. The main gap is the sixfold paediatric rise (claim 1).

least_plausible_claims.quote: Compounded product plus personal importation of Indian and Canadian generic semaglutide make the gray market an estimated 8–10% of US users.
least_plausible_claims.why: magnitude: 8–10% of roughly 38M users is 3–4M people. That is a jump from a 'contained' gray market, driven by a legal compounding window that lasted ten months and closed in Feb 2028, plus importation that is formally unauthorised. The estimate is asserted with no derivation.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Lilly raised Zepbound vial cash pricing from $349–499 to $399–549, citing demand and onshoring costs.
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: the semaglutide shortage hit Novo, not tirzepatide. A price rise by Lilly runs against the administration's negotiated price-cap deals and the 2026 trend toward ~$245, and no chain explains why the deal's terms did not bind.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Clinically meaningful in an estimated 1–3% of users, dose-related and usually reversible on dose reduction, according to 2027 pharmacovigilance analyses and one prospective cohort.
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: reward blunting goes from 'unquantified, trials not designed to detect it' to 'established', quantified, and on a label within two years. The only evidence given is unspecified pharmacovigilance and one cohort, and the manufacturer had 'no data to share'. This is faster and firmer than the niche_side_effect driver supports.

rationale.badness: The world is a recognisably harder society with new losers. Hourly workers are priced out by employer exits and cash prices of $199–499, and they turn to a gray market with contaminated imports (~3,400 adverse-event reports). Children on the drug have a growth signal and ~1.6× restrictive-eating diagnoses, and parents cannot tell whether stopping or continuing is riskier. Offsetting this, the signals are named, measured and labelled, and the state subsidises the poorest and the elderly, so epistemic harm is moderate and the world is not structurally hidden.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: All ten drivers are visible in the fields and events (adoption 14.9, shortage-driven price shock, employer 44%, the 6–11 label, the growth signal, the 50 mg oral, HRSA subsidy, 'unmedicated' movement, apathy on one label). Two are slightly stretched: a plant-failure supply shock sits awkwardly beside market_shock 'none', and anhedonia gains real political salience despite niche_side_effect. mechanism: Most chains are shown, such as the plant recall leading to the shortage, compounding and a regain natural experiment, and the oral approval following a head-to-head trial. Several links are asserted, including Lilly's price rise (claim 2), the near-instant quantification and labelling of apathy (claim 3), the unexplained HRSA funding source, and the 17-state Medicaid count. magnitude: Population figures sit inside the envelope (14.9 on drug, ever-used 21, income thirds weighting to ~14.8, age bands to ~15.0). The cycling arithmetic, Medicare $6.2B and HRSA $0.93B all multiply out, and the approval timing for CagriSema, retatrutide and survodutide follows the rules. Minor gaps: the $3B HRSA appropriation against ~$1.5–1.9B implied spend, the unsourced 8–10% gray-market share (claim 1), and survodutide's filing being absent from events.
rationale.generativity: The Marisol Treviño day is dense with concrete texture: the 5:40 pill and 30-minute wait, the sticker with the check-in date, the free-phone comparison, Ana's wall measurement, the foil-wrapped tortillas, and the 'unmedicated sunday' photo. The world fields add implied scenes such as dating-app fields, mismatched couples, EAP flatness guidance and Austin menu cards. Characters and conflicts (aide vs insured colleague, parent deciding about the dose) are clearly implied.

least_plausible_claims.quote: It requires growth monitoring every six months, and new paediatric starts fall ~30%.
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: a confounded EHR cohort in May 2028 turns into an FDA Drug Safety Communication with a monitoring mandate by August. A measured 30% drop in new starts is reported within the same month, which is implausibly fast.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The medical assistant measures Ana against the wall twice and writes 134.6. Last March it was 132.1.
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism/magnitude: about 2.5 cm over roughly 18 months is far below normal growth for a 10-year-old. The world's own signal is only ~0.8 cm/yr slower, and the doctor still calls it 'within range', so prose and world state disagree.

magnitude: this is roughly 3–4% of all children with obesity, against ~0.6% in 2026. That is a sixfold or greater jump in two years with no stated chain. The 6–11 cohort reaching ~70k within a year of the label is similarly abrupt.

rationale.badness: The world is a recognisably harder society with new losers. Employers retreat (44%), and hourly workers are priced out or pushed into a gray market with contaminated imports. Children carry an unresolved growth and restrictive-eating signal. Anhedonia has a label but is handled as a dose question, and the harms are named and measured, which holds epistemic badness down. Inequality is the main driver: the state covers the poorest, Medicare enrollees and Medicaid kids, and the hourly middle is left out. Cohesion takes a hit from mismatched couples, the 'unmedicated' politics and parents unable to decide for their kids.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is realised and traceable. Adoption lands exactly at +3.9pp, the shortage supplies the price shock, employer coverage falls to 44%, Wegovy gets a 6–11 label, the pediatric growth signal is in the ledger and events, oral 50 mg gives parity, HRSA is the subsidy, the unmedicated movement is the cultural response, and anhedonia stays a niche label item. mechanism: most chains are shown, including the plant failure, shortage, 503A reopening, gray market and regain natural experiment. The weak points are the three-month jump from a confounded cohort to a DSC with a measured 30% drop (claim 1) and Ana's growth numbers contradicting the stated effect size (claim 2). magnitude: all population figures sit inside the envelope (14.9 current, 21 ever), and the income and age bands weight back to ~15. The 520k × $149 × 12 ≈ $0.93B, 2.1M × $245 × 12 ≈ $6.2B and 510k pediatric figures all reconcile. The deductions are the unexplained pediatric jump (claim 3) and a $3B HRSA appropriation against only ~$1.5B of implied outlay over two years.
rationale.generativity: The prose follows Marisol through the 5:40 pill, the sticker with her check-in date, Mrs. Garza's son on Zepbound through the refinery, Ana's wall measurement and the tortillas wrapped back in foil. It ends on the unmedicated Sunday table and the sour gummies. The world fields add dating-app 'on/off/unmedicated' tags, 'unmedicated portions' menus, Medicare Advantage strength classes and PHQ-style apathy screens. That gives many implied scenes and characters.

least_plausible_claims.why: magnitude: the 2026 base was ~0.6% of children with obesity (roughly 90k children). A rise to ~510k implies about a sixfold jump in two years, and 0.7% of all under-18s implies roughly 3–4% of children with obesity, with no mechanism for the adolescent surge beyond the under-12 label.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Business Group on Health survey: 44% of large employers now cover GLP-1s for weight management, down from 60%.
least_plausible_claims.why: magnitude: a 16-point fall in one survey year is steeper than the 12-point fall in 2025–26. The text asserts it with no cost trigger beyond 'employer retreat', and the ~$499 cash-price rise points the other way for employer cost pressure.

least_plausible_claims.quote: It requires growth monitoring every six months, and new paediatric starts fall ~30%.
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism: a ~30% fall in new starts is dated to the same month as the Drug Safety Communication, so the effect appears at once with no chain through prescribers, Medicaid or parents. The underlying growth signal is also described as confounded.

rationale.badness: A recognisably harder society with new losers. Hourly workers sit in a hardening middle tier, paying $199–499 cash or using a gray market of 8–10% of users with ~3,400 adverse-event reports and contaminated imports. Children on Wegovy face an unresolved growth and restrictive-eating signal while their parents go uncovered. It is not worse than that, because the state backstops the poor and Medicare enrollees, anhedonia is measured and labelled (1–3%, reversible), and the harms are nameable, which lowers the epistemic score.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Every driver is visible in fields and events: the shortage price shock, 44% employer coverage, the 6–11 label, the growth signal, the oral 50 mg, the unmedicated movement, the HRSA subsidy and niche anhedonia. The Novo plant failure sits slightly uneasily with market_shock 'none', though it is the price_path mechanism. mechanism: Most chains are shown, including the shortage leading to compounding, the regain natural experiment, oral API demand and bottleneck, and Bridge enrollment leading to 65+ uptake. Weaker links are the same-month 30% drop in paediatric starts and the 16-point employer drop (claims 2 and 3), plus the label change appearing only on the 50 mg pill. magnitude: Adult on-drug (14.9), ever-used (21), income thirds (~14.8 weighted) and age bands (~15.0 weighted) are inside the envelope and reconcile, as do the cycling arithmetic, Medicare ($6.2B), HRSA ($0.93B) and approval timing. The main gap is the sixfold paediatric rise (claim 1).
